stem: According to the Salter-Harris classification, a Type II injury involves which of the following?

options.text: A fracture through the physis and the metaphysis.
A fracture isolated to the physis only.
A fracture through the physis and the epiphysis.
A crush injury to the physis.

explanation: Type II injuries involve the growth plate and an associated fragment of the metaphysis; they are the most common Salter-Harris type.
rationale: This is the most common type of physeal injury and involves the region 'beyond' the growth plate.

optionExplanations.A: Type II injuries involve the growth plate and an associated fragment of the metaphysis; they are the most common Salter-Harris type.
optionExplanations.B: An isolated injury to the physis without metaphysical or epiphysial fracture is classified as Type I.
optionExplanations.C: Injuries involving the physis and the epiphysis are intraarticular and classified as Type III.
optionExplanations.D: A compression or crush injury specifically involving the growth plate is classified as Type V.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: A fracture through the physis and the metaphysis.
